summary: Eszopiclone is an oral nonbenzodiazepine (cyclopyrrolone) hypnotic Z-drug indicated for the treatment of insomnia, where it decreases sleep latency and improves sleep maintenance. It acts at GABA-A receptor complexes near benzodiazepine binding domains. It carries a BOXED WARNING for complex sleep behaviors (sleep-walking, sleep-driving, and other activities while not fully awake) that may cause serious injury or death. It is a Schedule IV controlled substance with potential for dependence; dosing should use the lowest effective dose (max 3 mg, max 2 mg in elderly/debilitated or severe hepatic impairment / with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors), and patients must be cautioned about next-day impairment.
indications: Treatment of insomnia (decreases sleep latency and improves sleep maintenance)

dosage.d: Start 1 mg; may increase to 2 mg or 3 mg if clinically indicated (max 3 mg)
dosage.n: Take immediately before bedtime with at least 7-8 h remaining before awakening; lowest effective dose
Lower dose due to impaired motor/cognitive performance and increased sensitivity; higher fall risk

dosage.c: Insomnia - severe hepatic impairment or potent CYP3A4 inhibitor use
dosage.n: Dose reduction required; use with caution

admin: Only take when able to stay in bed a full night (7-8 hours) before being active again
Do NOT take with or immediately after a meal (especially high-fat) - slows absorption and reduces effect on sleep latency
Do NOT take if alcohol was consumed that evening
Use the lowest effective dose; caution patients on 3 mg against next-day driving/activities requiring full alertness
Discontinue immediately if a complex sleep behavior occurs
moa: The mechanism of action as a hypnotic is not fully established, but eszopiclone (a cyclopyrrolone, the S-isomer of zopiclone) is thought to act through interaction with GABA-A receptor complexes at binding domains located close to or allosterically coupled to benzodiazepine receptors, enhancing GABA-mediated inhibitory neurotransmission.

absolute: Patients who have experienced complex sleep behaviors after taking eszopiclone
Known hypersensitivity to eszopiclone (reactions include anaphylaxis and angioedema)
relative: History of alcohol or drug abuse, or psychiatric disorder - greater risk of abuse/dependence (Schedule IV controlled substance)
Concomitant CNS depressants (benzodiazepines, opioids, tricyclics) or alcohol - additive depression
Severe hepatic impairment or use of potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (limit to 2 mg)
Elderly or debilitated (limit to 2 mg; fall risk)
monitor: Emergence of complex sleep behaviors - discontinue immediately if they occur
Signs of abuse, tolerance, or dependence (Schedule IV)
Abnormal thinking and behavioral changes (decreased inhibition, agitation, depersonalization)
Persistence of insomnia beyond 7-10 days (reevaluate for comorbid disorder)

preg: Available pharmacovigilance data in pregnant women are insufficient to identify a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse outcomes. Animal reproduction studies in rats and rabbits showed no teratogenicity, but offspring toxicities (increased post-implantation loss, decreased pup weight/survival, increased startle response) occurred when given throughout pregnancy and lactation at doses approximately 200 times the MRHD. Use only if the benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: There are no data on the presence of eszopiclone in human or animal milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or effects on milk production. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother's clinical need for eszopiclone and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant.
renal: No dose adjustment is necessary in renal impairment. AUC and Cmax are similar to matched healthy controls because less than 10% of an oral dose is excreted unchanged in the urine.
hepatic: Exposure is increased approximately 2-fold in severe hepatic impairment. No dose adjustment is necessary for mild-to-moderate impairment, but in severe hepatic impairment the dose should not exceed 2 mg, and eszopiclone should be used with caution.

major: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, nefazodone, troleandomycin, ritonavir, nelfinavir) - increase eszopiclone exposure; limit dose to 2 mg
Other CNS depressants (benzodiazepines, opioids, tricyclic antidepressants) - additive CNS depression; downward dose adjustment of both may be needed
moderate: Alcohol (ethanol) - additive psychomotor impairment; do not use eszopiclone if alcohol consumed that evening
Olanzapine - pharmacodynamic interaction with decreased DSST scores (no PK change)
Potent CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin) - may markedly decrease eszopiclone exposure and effect
minor: No clinically significant interaction with paroxetine
interactions.food: Taking with or immediately after a high-fat/heavy meal slows absorption, reduces Cmax ~21%, and delays Tmax ~1 h, reducing effect on sleep onset; do not take with or immediately after a meal.
interactions.alcohol: Additive psychomotor impairment and CNS depression; fatalities with overdose have occurred only in combination with other CNS drugs or alcohol. Advise patients not to take eszopiclone if they drank alcohol that evening.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic interference reported; consider monitoring methemoglobin in high-dose overdose (methemoglobinemia reported with racemic zopiclone).

Next-day impairment of alertness, motor coordination, and driving (especially at 2-3 mg)

counsel: Take only as prescribed, right before getting into bed, and only when able to stay in bed 7-8 hours
Eszopiclone may cause complex sleep behaviors (sleep-walking, sleep-driving, eating, phone calls, sex) while not fully awake - stop the drug and contact your provider immediately if this happens
Next-day impairment can occur even when you feel fully awake; do not drive or perform alert-requiring tasks the day after a 3 mg dose
Do not drink alcohol that evening; tell your provider about all medicines and substances you take
Do not increase the dose on your own; this medicine can be habit forming
Read the Medication Guide with each prescription and refill
Report any suicidal thoughts, severe allergic reactions, or unusual behavior immediately
Do not take with or immediately after a meal
pk: Rapidly absorbed; peak in ~1 hour, supporting use immediately before bedtime
Tmax ~1 hour (delayed ~1 hour by high-fat meal)
Terminal elimination half-life ~6 hours (~9 hours in the elderly)
Supports overnight sleep; higher 2-3 mg morning levels increase next-day impairment risk
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F) [USP Controlled Room Temperature]
pearls: BOXED WARNING: Complex sleep behaviors (sleep-walking, sleep-driving, and other activities while not fully awake) may occur after the first or any dose and can cause serious injury or death - discontinue immediately if they occur; contraindicated thereafter.
Habit forming: Yes - Schedule IV controlled substance; risk of dependence, complex sleep behaviors, and next-day impairment
Next-day impairment can occur even when used as prescribed and even when the patient feels fully awake, especially at 2-3 mg; caution against driving the morning after a 3 mg dose
Additive CNS depression with alcohol and other CNS depressants; fatal overdoses have occurred only with other CNS drugs or alcohol
Metabolized by CYP3A4 (and CYP2E1) - limit to 2 mg with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors; rifampicin markedly lowers levels
No renal dose adjustment (<10% excreted unchanged); severe hepatic impairment and elderly limited to 2 mg
Flumazenil may be useful in overdose
missed: Eszopiclone is taken only at bedtime when a full night of sleep (7-8 hours) is available. If a dose is missed, skip it - do not take it during the night or the next day. Never double the dose.
overdose: Overdose presents as exaggerated CNS depression ranging from somnolence to coma; methemoglobinemia has been reported with racemic zopiclone. Single overdoses up to 36 mg (clinical trials) and up to 270 mg (postmarketing) have been survived; fatalities occurred only in combination with other CNS drugs or alcohol. Treatment is symptomatic and supportive: gastric lavage where appropriate, IV fluids, monitoring of respiration, pulse, and blood pressure, treatment of hypotension and CNS depression. Flumazenil may be useful. Consider monitoring methemoglobin in high-dose overdose. The value of dialysis is not established; consider multiple-drug ingestion and contact a poison control center.
